# Q1

1(a) Lead with a one-sentence answer to the prompt. Then give the example or evidence, and end with the reasoning the prompt asks for (Author, Year).

1(b) Lead with a one-sentence answer. Define key terms briefly, such as $\Delta\theta$, then describe each method or step in its own short paragraph.

*Method or point one.* One to three sentences.

*Method or point two.* One to three sentences.

Comparison or conclusion in two to four sentences.

References

```{=latex}
\begingroup\footnotesize
```

Author, A. A., & Author, B. B. (Year). Title of article. *Journal Name, Volume*(Issue), pages. https://doi.org/xxxx

```{=latex}
\endgroup
```

# Q3

3(a) Answer. Use a compact table only when it is the clearest way to compare items:

|   | Option A | Option B |
|------------------|------------------|------------------|
| Property 1 | ... | ... |
| Property 2 | ... | ... |

3(b) Answer, with a figure drawn by R code. Set `echo: true` in the chunk to show the code.

```{r}
#| label: fig-q3b
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 4.2
#| out-width: "55%"
#| fig-cap: "Stand-alone caption describing the expected result and what it shows."
x <- seq(0, 10, length.out = 200)
plot(x, pnorm(x, 5, 1), type = "l", lwd = 2, las = 1, bty = "l",
     xlab = "Stimulus value", ylab = "Proportion of responses")
abline(h = 0.5, lty = 3, col = "gray60")
```

References

```{=latex}
\begingroup\footnotesize
```

Author, A. A., Author, B. B., & Author, C. C. (Year). Title of article. *Journal Name, Volume*, pages.

```{=latex}
\endgroup
```
